segments.content:
Chapter 104: Great Hero Chen's Two Companies Both Have Good Names

After class, Professor Yuan left directly.

Even some students who had been listening from the hallway swarmed up to ask him questions, as they didn't have a chance to ask during class.

Seeing the large crowd, Chen Guiliang didn't go over to join in, but he too was surrounded by some classmates.

"Chen Guiliang, what's your MSN?"

"Sorry, I only have QQ."

"Then leave your QQ or email. We can chat more when we have time. I'm also a big fan of ancient literature."

"My QQ and email are..."

"Classmate, do you have a cell phone? Can I get your number?"

"Let's just stick to online communication."

"Have you been writing any poetry lately? I write classical poetry on the school BBS's 'poem' board. We could compare notes. What's your BBS username?"

"I've never logged into the Peking University BBS before."

"How can a Peking University student not use the Peking University BBS? You should go check it out. My username is Qingfeng Lanyue."

"Alright, I'll go tonight."

"Classmate Chen Guiliang, I wrote four ci poems during the National Day holiday. I'll email them to you tonight when I get back to the dorm. Help me polish them up."

"I wouldn't presume to polish them. Let's discuss them together."

The students who came to audit "Ancient Chinese Literature" were, more or less, all interested in the subject.

Some of them were already writing their own classical-style poems and ci.

It was a small circle, and very few were highly skilled. They had a strong desire to connect and were exceptionally enthusiastic when they met a kindred spirit, even capable of pulling you into a rambling chat for an hour or two.

Chen Guiliang was very patient at this moment, publicly sharing his QQ and email address and conversing politely with all the students.

But there were too many people, so Chen Guiliang was unwilling to give out his phone number.

The people who had gathered around not only talked with Chen Guiliang but also started chatting among themselves, exchanging contact information.

The place had turned into a large-scale offline meetup.

Chen Guiliang smiled happily. Before him were all potential users of Three Kingdoms Kill and Xiaonei!

He left the Liberal Arts Education Building in high spirits. Zhao Beibei and the other Yuanpei Program students caught up with him, talking and laughing about the ancient myths discussed in class today.

Soon, Chen Guiliang's smile vanished.

There were fixed bicycle racks along the main entrance and surrounding paths of the Liberal Arts Education Building. Chen Guiliang had arrived rather late, and the racks outside the main entrance were already full, so he had temporarily locked his bike in an open area in front of the building.

Although it wasn't a proper parking spot, everyone did it. Especially for the first class in the morning, the number of improperly parked bikes could block the road.

At this very moment, the spot where he had parked his bike was completely empty...

"Who the fuck stole my bike!"

Chen Guiliang cursed in anger, "Stealing a crappy second-hand bike that costs a few dozen yuan? That son of a bitch must be desperate for money!"

"Hahahaha!"

The classmates who had just been asking him for his contact information were now laughing uproariously at his misfortune.

Zhao Beibei patted his shoulder, "My condolences. It's possible the one you bought was also stolen and sold. Now it's just re-entered the second-hand market."

"Is that your way of comforting me?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"Yes," Zhao Beibei nodded.

"You're really good at comforting people." Chen Guiliang wanted to trick this guy into wearing women's clothes; with his fair skin, he'd probably be popular with a lot of perverts.

A sophomore shixiong pushing a bicycle came over, "Shidi, you're still too young. Look at my bike, a full five locks. Even a bike thief would shake his head and walk away."

"Thank you for the advice, Shixiong."

Chen Guiliang walked back to the dorm gloomily, planning to buy an even crappier bike, the kind that would make a thief weep upon seeing it.

In dorm room 404, he was still the only one there.

Guo Feng slept at the office every day.

Min-shixiong and Jiang Junlai, on the other hand, timed their return to the dorm. Unless they needed to do laundry or shower, they would stay in the study room until the very last minute.

Chen Guiliang turned on his computer. He didn't start writing right away, but first went to browse the Peking University BBS.

At this time, non-students could also post freely on university BBS forums, which was how Sister Furong had exploded in popularity this year. It wouldn't be until next year, in response to policy directives, that they would switch to a real-name system for campus users.

When Chen Guiliang registered for an account, he didn't know what username to pick, so he just randomly went with "Feng Kelian."

He quickly browsed the posts and found that the Society and Economics boards had an astonishing number of posts recently. Clicking in, he saw that, my goodness, most of them were discussing the reform of state-owned enterprises.

This topic was thrown out by Larry Lang last year and had grown into a national discussion by this year.

Influenced by public opinion, the MBOs of state-owned enterprises would be halted next year.

It directly changed the direction of state-owned enterprise reform!

Chen Guiliang also enjoyed being a keyboard warrior. After reading a few posts, his fingers started to itch, and he couldn't help but tap out a couple of comments.

He then went into the Literature and Arts board and saw someone had posted a question: "I just read 'Legends of Ancient and Modern,' and the author of that story 'Wulin Inn' is Bu Feiyan. Is that the same person from our BBS?"

"That's her, a first-year master's student, specializing in ancient literature."

"I was wondering why she hadn't been active lately. Turns out she went into seclusion to write a novel."

"Sigh, Shuxia Yehou has also been missing for a long time. I used to see him on the BBS occasionally."

"The author of 'Chronicles of the God-Seekers' is our shixiong too?"

"An alumnus. He graduated a long time ago."

"I read 'Mengya' during the National Day holiday. Chen Guiliang's 'Those Things About the Ming Dynasty' is quite interesting."

"What? You're in university and you're still reading 'Mengya'? That's for middle school students."

"Why can't university students read it?"

Chen Guiliang then clicked into the Original Works board. Thinking of his stolen bicycle, he couldn't resist posting a doggerel poem.

"To the Bicycle Thief"

Covered in rust, its bell long mute,

Tires leaking, seat falling to boot.

You'd even stoop to take this wreck,

You must be fucking crazy broke!

A post like this was surprisingly popular, and a bunch of replies appeared quickly.

"Haha, another victim."

"Great poem, great poem!"

"I miss my beloved bike of two years. May the bike thief's son be born without an asshole!"

"The bike thief won't even find a wife, what son is he gonna have."

"Brother, you are a great talent. This poem may seem vulgar, but it holds a hidden depth, voicing the feelings of us students whose bikes have been stolen in a humorous tone... To hell with it, my bike that I bought for several hundred yuan was also stolen by some idiot during the National Day holiday!"

This post soon became a support group for victims of bicycle theft.

Chen Guiliang found it hilarious. Clicking into other boards, he accidentally stumbled upon Sister Furong's post. Her S-shaped figure was a bit hard on the eyes, scaring him into quickly logging off the BBS to write his manuscript.

He had already collected and transcribed all the interesting historical materials about Zhu Yuanzhang.

Now he just had to string them together with humorous words. His fingers flew across the keyboard, typing rapidly.

"Writing your historical novel again?"

Min-shixiong and Jiang Junlai finally returned. Any later and they would have been marked down for a late return.

Jiang Junlai was so tired his head was spinning. He lay on his bed and grumbled, "Even my third year of high school wasn't this busy!"

Chen Guiliang laughed, "You got recommended for admission through the Math Olympiad. What could you have been busy with in your third year?"

"Busy learning advanced mathematics," Jiang Junlai said.

"You're something else." Chen Guiliang didn't want to continue this damn topic.

Min Wenyu asked, "Lately, publishing houses have been calling you all the time. Did 'Those Things About the Ming Dynasty' get sold?"

"It's sold," Chen Guiliang said.

Min Wenyu said, "For how much?"

Chen Guiliang said, "A tiered royalty starting at a guaranteed 15%."

Neither Min-shixiong nor Jiang Junlai knew anything about the publishing industry, so they didn't understand what this offer meant. After a brief chat, they moved on to other topics.

Chen Guiliang continued to tap away at his keyboard.

After writing three or four thousand words, Chen Guiliang rubbed his wrists. "Min-shixiong, do you know any seniors from the law school?"

"Plenty," said Min Wenyu. "A quarter of the students from our 2003 Yuanpei class are majoring in law."

Chen Guiliang said, "They wouldn't have a problem looking over a contract, would they?"

"What do you think?" Min Wenyu retorted.

"Introduce me to one. I need to sign a contract tomorrow."

"Alright. You'll have to treat them to a meal."

"No problem. Let's all go for a big meal tomorrow night. You and Jiang Junlai can come too."

Jiang Junlai let out a sigh, "Aigh, I have class tomorrow night."

Chen Guiliang laughed, "Who told you to sign up for 20 courses?"

Jiang Junlai said wearily, "I regret it. But the add/drop period is over, so I can't drop any classes now."

The shixiong Min Wenyu introduced was named Xu Lei, a 2002 Yuanpei class student majoring in law, with minors in management, philosophy, and sociology.

"There are no major issues, just a few details that need to be changed." Xu Lei circled a few words with his pen.

Li Xunhuan took the contract, glanced at it, and smiled. "Then let's just print out two new copies nearby."

They found a print shop. Chen Guiliang signed and pressed his thumbprint, and Li Xunhuan signed and stamped it with the company seal.

Next, they went to the bank, and the 100,000 yuan advance was transferred to Chen Guiliang's account.

"I have to go now," said Li Xunhuan.

Chen Guiliang said, "Let's go get some barbecue together."

Li Xunhuan replied, "Next time. I really have something urgent to attend to."

"Alright then, see you."

"See you."

Chen Guiliang went for barbecue with Xu Lei-shixiong and also called Min-shixiong to join them.

Sitting at the barbecue stall, Xu Lei couldn't help but ask, "What's the deal with your book? A guaranteed 15% tiered royalty. I must be out of touch, because I've never heard of anyone getting such a high royalty rate."

Chen Guiliang explained simply, "A small shark has swum into the publishing world."

"I see," Xu Lei nodded.

Don't be fooled by how casually Li Xunhuan spoke, even saying that Guo Xiaosi's photo book was destined for low sales, which was why he didn't offer an ultra-high price.

That was all bullshit.

His offer to Guo Xiaosi was definitely also a guaranteed 15% with a tiered royalty. To secure that deal, Li Xunhuan had frequently traveled between Beijing and Shanghai, personally convincing the plagiarized party to settle with Guo Xiaosi.

However, Guo Xiaosi still felt Li Xunhuan's company was unreliable and ultimately chose the traditional publisher with the second-highest offer.

If Chen Guiliang wasn't a reincarnator, he would have also chosen Chunfeng Literature and Art Publishing House...

That editor, Shi Xiang, made perfect sense with everything he said, and he was exceptionally sincere.

Only Han Han was bold enough to take a risk and cooperate with Li Xunhuan.

The second week after Chen Guiliang signed the publishing contract, his two companies finally completed their registration.

One company was called Game Science.

The other was called ByteDance.

Guo Feng particularly liked these two names. He looked at the business licenses and said, "They sound great. Especially ByteDance, it has a kind of STEM-student romance to it. Let's hurry and have two signs made. I'll take a picture to show my shijie."

This guy had recently bought a film camera.

(End of Chapter)
